extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for reviewers evaluating technical paper submissions to SIGGRAPH Asia 2016, covering evaluation criteria, ethics, double‑blind procedure, format requirements, timeliness, and post‑review handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical soundness and substantial contribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Each paper that is accepted must be technically sound and make a substantial contribution to the field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minor flaws can be corrected and shouldn't be a reason to reject a paper. Familiarize yourself with the Call for Submissions to understand what counts as a substantial contribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Look for what's good or stimulating
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and highlight the positive, interesting, or stimulating aspects of the paper as part of your review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize strengths as well as weaknesses; framing what is valuable in a submission helps the committee and authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics and professionalism (confidentiality & conduct)
rubrics_metrics.description: Uphold reputation for treating ideas confidentially and professionally; follow the Ethics of Review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By accepting a paper you guarantee to review materials in approved formats; if you are unwilling to do so, recuse yourself. Maintain professional conduct in all communications and protect confidential material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to review approved formats (media/format requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers guarantee to review materials submitted in approved formats: PDF for documents; QuickTime MPEG‑4 and DivX Version 6 for videos (check for an audio track); TIFF, PNG, or JPG for images.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you are not willing to review these formats, recuse yourself. You are expected to make a reasonable effort to review materials in non‑approved formats, but you are not under the same absolute obligation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double‑blind review practice and anonymity protection
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewing is double‑blind: authors hide names/affiliations/acks; reviewers' identities are not disclosed to authors. Reviewers must write reviews and bulletin communications so their identity remains protected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be careful in wording to avoid revealing or implying your identity. Follow double‑blind norms when discussing prior work and personal involvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling prior availability / prior art under double‑blind
rubrics_metrics.description: If the paper builds on ideas previously available (e.g., SIGGRAPH Asia Sketch, Briefs, talk, technical report, thesis), that previous availability should not be considered prior art for the authors of the previously available material but should be considered prior art otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because of double‑blind you may not know which case applies; explicitly state how your evaluation would differ if the paper author were the same person as the author of the previous material (example: "If the paper author is the poster author, my score is 4 ... If the paper author is not the poster author, my score is 2.").

rubrics_metrics.name: Be specific, detailed, and cite sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews should be specific and detailed. In discussions of related work, cite specific publications or public disclosures rather than saying 'this is well known'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Explanation section is often the most important part of the review—sometimes more important than the score. Thorough discussion helps the Papers Committee decide which papers to accept, and the review returned to authors should include specific feedback on ways to improve. See Greg Turk's 'Writing Technical Reviews' for more suggestions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanation section importance relative to score
rubrics_metrics.description: The Explanation section of your review can be more influential than the numeric score when the Papers Committee makes decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide detailed reasoning and constructive suggestions; do not rely solely on your numeric score to convey your assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the online review system correctly
rubrics_metrics.description: Access papers and supplemental material through the online submission/review system using your standard submission account and the 'Access the Jury/Review System' link.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have questions or problems with the online review system, contact the SIGGRAPH Asia Technical Papers Administrator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use provided library resources
rubrics_metrics.description: ACM and Eurographics provide full access to their Digital Libraries for SIGGRAPH Asia paper reviewer usage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You must log in (credentials provided via the electronic review system) to access the full text of articles; you are encouraged to make full use of these resources to inform your review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness of reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete and submit reviews by the stated deadline (03 July 2016 23:59 UTC/GMT unless a senior reviewer sets an earlier deadline).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhering to the deadline is extremely important because the Papers Committee has significant post‑review work. There will be an author rebuttal process preceding the Papers Committee meeting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post‑review handling and retention of materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers may keep copies of papers, notes, marked manuscripts, or implementations because of a process for revised papers where authors can release previous reviewers' names and resubmissions may be reassigned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you keep materials, insulate ideas learned from the review from your own research and from colleagues and students. Be aware your reviews and any materials may be perused by future SIGGRAPH Asia reviewers.
